examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Compute E[X]=sum xp(x) or its integral and Var(X)=E[X²]−E[X]². Linearity of expectation requires no independence, whereas adding variances requires zero covariance. For a transformation aX+b, the mean transforms linearly and variance scales by a²; the additive constant contributes no variance.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
X has variance 5. What is Var(3X−7)?

**Answer: 45.** Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X). Thus Var(3X−7)=9·5=45. Shifting every value by −7 changes the mean but not deviations about that mean.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
E[XY]=E[X]E[Y] is not generally valid for dependent variables. An expected subinterval length must weight the event selecting that interval, as in the supplied random-cut PYQ.

E[g(X)] is generally not g(E[X]) for nonlinear g.
